beats.intro: Long expressions can often be made shorter. [[q]]The trick is to spot terms that are alike, and put them together.
beats.tiles: Let's use tiles to picture terms. [[x]]A long bar stands for x. [[x2]]A big square stands for x squared: an x by x square. [[one]]And a small square stands for one. [[neg]]A red outline means the tile is negative.
beats.like: Like terms have the same variable raised to the same exponent. [[l1]]Three a squared and seven a squared are like terms. [[l2]]Four x and nine y are not: the variables are different. [[l3]]Eight p and eight p to the seventh are not like terms either: the exponents are different. [[coef]]The coefficients don't matter. Only the variable part has to match.
beats.combine: To combine like terms, add their coefficients. [[q]]Simplify seven x minus two x plus four x. [[show]]Here are seven x bars, [[neg]]two negative x bars, [[pos]]and four more x bars. [[cancel]]Each negative bar cancels a positive one. [[count]]Nine x bars are left. [[ans]]So seven minus two plus four is nine: the answer is nine x.
beats.mixed: When there are different kinds of terms, group each kind separately. [[q]]Simplify three x squared minus eight x plus one plus seven x minus ten x squared. [[sort]]Slide the tiles into groups: x squared tiles, x tiles, and ones. [[sq]]Three minus ten is negative seven: negative seven x squared. [[xs]]Negative eight plus seven is negative one: negative x. [[c]]And the one stays. [[ans]]The result is negative seven x squared minus x plus one, in standard form.
beats.cant: Terms that are not alike stay separate. [[q]]In seven a minus eight b plus thirteen c plus five a plus b minus two, [[a]]seven a and five a combine to twelve a. [[b]]Negative eight b and b combine to negative seven b. [[rest]]Thirteen c and negative two have no partners, so they stay. [[ans]]The result is twelve a minus seven b plus thirteen c minus two.
beats.dist: Sometimes you need the distributive property first. [[q]]Simplify two plus eleven x minus three times x minus five. [[d]]Share the negative three with both terms inside: negative three x, and negative three times negative five, which is plus fifteen. [[group]]Now combine: eleven x minus three x is eight x, [[c]]and two plus fifteen is seventeen. [[ans]]The result is eight x plus seventeen.
beats.wrap: Like terms have the same variables with the same exponents. [[w1]]Combine them by adding their coefficients, keeping each sign. [[w2]]Terms that are not alike stay separate. [[w3]]Distribute first if there are parentheses, and write the result in standard form. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
beats.final2: Next, decide whether each pair is made of like terms.
beats.final3: Last one. Simplify with the distributive property.
beats.finish: Well done. That's the end of chapter twenty-three, combining like terms.
